evidence.title: Zhangye Railway Station
evidence.text: Zhangye Railway Station is located 6.4 km north east of Zhangye, Gansu.

evidence.title: Zhangye Railway Station
evidence.text: It handles about 49 passenger services per day along the Lanzhou–Xinjiang Railway as well as being a major freight depot.

evidence.title: Zhangye Ganzhou Airport
evidence.text: Zhangye Ganzhou Airport (IATA: YZY, ICAO: ZLZY) , or Zhangye Southeast Air Base, is a dual-use military and civil airport serving the city of Zhangye in Gansu Province, China.

evidence.title: Zhangye Ganzhou Airport
evidence.text: It is located 24 kilometers from the city center.

evidence.title: Zhangye Ganzhou Airport
evidence.text: Construction began in May 2010 to convert the air base to a dual-use airport, at an estimated cost of 313 million yuan.

evidence.title: Zhangye Ganzhou Airport
evidence.text: The airport was opened on 1 November 2011.

evidence.title: The Nan'ao General Headquarters
evidence.text: The Nan'ao General Headquarters (南澳总兵府) is located in Nan'ao County, Shantou, Guangdong province, China.

evidence.title: The Nan'ao General Headquarters
evidence.text: It served as a military center for coastal defense of Guangdong, Fujian province, and Taiwan.

evidence.title: The Nan'ao General Headquarters
evidence.text: Now the Headquarters is used as a museum of coast defense.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: Nan (Thai: น่าน ,  ] ) is a town in northern Thailand.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: It is 668 km north of Bangkok.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: It is in the centre of Nan Province which bears its name, and of which it is the former administrative capital.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: It covers the whole "tambon" Nai Wiang and parts of "tambon" Pha Sing of Mueang Nan district, an area of 7.60 km².

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: In 2010 it had a population of 21,333.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: It is subdivided into 30 "chumchon".

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: It is spread along the Nan River's right bank.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: Nan is a small city, primarily devoted to commercial, administrative, educational, and hospital activities.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: The old heart of the city, where Wat Phumin, the national museum and other tourist attractions are located, is being restored.

evidence.title: Nan, Thailand
evidence.text: The city's industrial and tourist development remains limited until now, but should be improved by the complete opening of the border towards Laos and beyond towards China.

evidence.title: Zhangye
evidence.text: Zhangye, formerly romanized as Changyeh or known as Kanchow, is a prefecture-level city in central Gansu Province in the People's Republic of China.

evidence.title: Zhangye
evidence.text: It borders Inner Mongolia on the north and Qinghai on the south.

evidence.title: Zhangye
evidence.text: Its central district is Ganzhou, formerly a city of the Western Xia and one of the most important outposts of western China.

evidence.title: Zhangye West Railway Station
evidence.text: Zhangye West Railway Station () is a railway station located in China's Gansu Province, Zhangye City, Ganzhou District.

evidence.title: Zhangye West Railway Station
evidence.text: It was put into operation on December 26, 2014.

evidence.title: Zhangye West Railway Station
evidence.text: It serves the Lanzhou–Xinjiang High-Speed Railway with High Speed services between Lanzhou and Urumqi and conventional services connecting Urumqi to various cities in Eastern and South Western China.

evidence.title: Zhangye West Railway Station
evidence.text: It is the second railway station serving Zhangye, with Zhangye Railway Station which serves the conventional LanXin Railway.

evidence.title: Zhangye National Geopark
evidence.text: The Gansu Zhangye National Geopark (, herein, the ″Zhangye National Geopark″), is located in Sunan and Linze counties within the prefecture-level city of Zhangye.

evidence.title: Zhangye National Geopark
evidence.text: It covers an area of 322 km2 .

evidence.title: Zhangye National Geopark
evidence.text: The site became a quasi-national geopark on April 23, 2012 (provisional name: Gansu Zhangye Danxia Geopark).

evidence.title: Zhangye National Geopark
evidence.text: It was formally designated as ″Gansu Zhangye National Geopark″ by the Ministry of Land and Resources on June 16, 2016 after it has passed the on-site acceptance test.

evidence.title: Zhangye National Geopark
evidence.text: Known for its colorful rock formations, it has been voted by Chinese media outlets as one of the most beautiful landforms in China.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: The Rally China (中國拉力賽) is the largest rally racing event held in China.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: The first event was run as the "China Rally" in 1997 in the province of Guangdong, as a replacement to the Hong Kong - Beijing Rally, and was an event on the World Rally Championship (WRC) calendar in 1999.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: However it was replaced by the Cyprus Rally the following year.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: From 2000 to 2015, it has been part of the Asia Pacific Rally Championship (APRC), moving initially to Shaoguan, Fujian province. "

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: "Force majeure because of government"", according to the organisers, led to the cancellation of the event in 2003.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: The event moved for a single year to Huizhou, Guangdong in 2004 before reverting to Shaoguan.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: From 2009 until 2015, the event was hosted in Longyou, Zhejiang province.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: The event will return to the WRC calendar in 2016 after moving to Huairou, Beijing.

evidence.title: Rally China
evidence.text: China will continue to host a round of the Asia-Pacific Rally Championship in Zhangye, Gansu in 2016 too, while Longyou will continue to host a round of the Chinese Rally Championship.

evidence.title: Nan'an, Fujian
evidence.text: Nan'an () is a county-level city of southern Fujian province, People's Republic of China.

evidence.title: Nan'an, Fujian
evidence.text: It is under the administration of Quanzhou City and as of 2010, had a total population of 1,500,000.

evidence.title: Nan'an, Fujian
evidence.text: More than 3,000,000 overseas Chinese trace their ancestry to Nan'an.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: Fujian Medical University () is a university located in Fuzhou, Fujian, China.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: Fujian Medical University was founded in1937, named Fujian Provincial Medical Vocational School at that time.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: The name of the school was changed to Fujian Provincial Medical College in 1939 and was called Fujian Medical College in 1949.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: In 1969, after merging with Fujian Chinese Traditional Medical College and the medical department of Huaqiao University, Fujian Medical University was founded and moved to Quanzhou, Fujian.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: It was moved back to Fuzhou in 1978.

evidence.title: Fujian Medical University
evidence.text: The name of the school was changed back to Fujian Medical College in 1982 and then changed back to the present name in April 1996.
